title: "The pipeline"
---

## The question

**Did Latino voters in the Western states shift toward Trump between 2020 and 2024, and
does authoritarianism condition that shift?**

Western States Survey (YouGov), 2020 (n = 3,600) and 2024 (n = 4,000): Arizona,
Colorado, Nevada, New Mexico, Utah. Codebooks:
[2020](codebooks/wss2020_codebook.pdf), [2024](codebooks/wss2024_codebook.pdf).

- `latino` — the YouGov `race` item (Hispanic).
- `authoritarianism` — mean of four child-rearing pairs, 0–1, 1 = authoritarian
  response (`auth1`–`auth4`).
- `trump_vote` — 1 Trump, 0 Biden/Harris, `NA` otherwise.
- Weights — `weight` in 2020, `weight_all` in 2024, combined as `weight`.

::: {.note}
[Cite the codebook, not the agent]{.note-head}
Every claim about a variable on this page traces to `codebooks/` and the variable list
in `AGENTS.md`. When an agent tells you what a variable means, that is a hypothesis.
:::

| Stage | File | Produces | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build | `R/00_build_data.R` | `data/wss_2020_2024.csv` (raw files not distributed) | [The data](06-data.qmd) |
| Recode | `R/01_recode.R` | `data/wss_clean.rds` | [The recode](07-recode.qmd) |
| Analyze | `R/02_analysis.R` | `output/*.png`, model summaries | [The analysis](08-analysis.qmd) |
| Check | `tests/testthat/` | pass / fail | [The tests](09-tests.qmd) |
| Explore | `app/app.R` | interactive app | [The app](10-app-and-publishing.qmd) |
| Publish | `quarto publish gh-pages` | this book | [Publishing](10-app-and-publishing.qmd) |

The chapters that follow run these scripts, so their tables and figures are whatever the
code currently produces — not transcriptions of a run from some earlier afternoon.

## Run it end to end

```bash
Rscript R/01_recode.R                       # csv  -> data/wss_clean.rds
Rscript R/02_analysis.R                     # models, figures -> output/
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'
Rscript -e 'shiny::runApp("app")'
```

`R/00_build_data.R` needs the raw Stata files, which are not distributed; the CSV it
produces is in the repository.

::: {.note}
[Why the order is enforced]{.note-head}
Every number traces back through exactly one path. If the recode changes, the analysis
and the app change with it, because neither keeps its own private copy of the recoding
logic. Ask an agent to add a recode to `02_analysis.R` and it will happily do it — this
is the rule you are enforcing against your own convenience.
:::

## Where we start

Weighted two-party Trump share:

| | 2020 | 2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Latino | .503 (n = 1,944) | .511 (n = 2,828) | +.008 |
| Latino | .398 (n = 937) | .419 (n = 786) | +.021 |

```{r}
#| label: headline
#| echo: false
library(tidyverse)
if (!file.exists("data/wss_clean.rds")) source("R/01_recode.R")
wss <- read_rds("data/wss_clean.rds")
voters <- filter(wss, !is.na(trump_vote))
voters |>
  summarise(trump = weighted.mean(trump_vote, weight), n = n(),
            .by = c(year, latino)) |>
  arrange(latino, year) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(trump, n)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
               caption = "Recomputed on every render, from data/wss_clean.rds.")
```

```{r}
#| label: ns
#| echo: false
c(n_obs = nrow(voters), n_miss = nrow(wss) - nrow(voters), n_total = nrow(wss))
```

n_miss here is non-voters, other candidates, and the ineligible — everyone for whom a
two-party vote is undefined.

::: {.warn}
[The puzzle]{.warn-head}
A two-point Latino shift, estimated on 786 Latino respondents in 2024, is far from the
double-digit national exit-poll story. Sample? Weights? Mode? Reported versus intended
vote? That is the interesting part — not reproducing a headline, but establishing what
this sample can and cannot support.
:::

Source: `R/02_analysis.R` run on `data/wss_clean.rds`. The intervals in that script use
a Kish effective *n*, not a design-based variance — fixing that would be a reasonable
first change to make.

## Four directions this could go

Any one of these is a complete demonstration of the loop — prompt, diff, `n_obs`, test.
We walk through one; the rest are here to run later, on this repo or your own data.

1. **Recode** — add generation, income terciles, and a strength-of-partisanship measure
   to `R/01_recode.R`. Check each against the codebook, and add a test per variable.
2. **Analysis** — Bayesian logit with `brms`; predicted probabilities for
   authoritarianism × Latino × year. Does the reported/intended distinction
   (`vote_type`) matter?
3. **Shiny** — add a state-by-year panel and a download button to `app/app.R`.
4. **Skepticism** — is this sample representative of Latino voters? Interrogate the
   weights, the mode, and the comparison with external estimates.

::: {.turn}
[The loop, whichever you pick]{.turn-head}
Branch → prompt the agent → **read the diff** → report `n_obs` and `n_miss` → write the
test → commit. All of it in your own clone.
:::

## Starting prompts worth stealing

```text
Read AGENTS.md and R/01_recode.R. Add an income-tercile variable built from
faminc, using survey weights. Do not touch anything else. Show me the diff.

Read codebooks/wss2024_codebook.pdf for pid7 and tell me whether
R/01_recode.R codes party3 correctly. Quote the codebook.

Refit the model in R/02_analysis.R with brms, bernoulli family, weakly
informative priors. Report n_obs and n_miss. Do not drop the weights.
```

Each of these is narrow, names its files, and asks for evidence. That is the whole
technique.
